assessment.title: Shakespeare and Post-1914 Literature (1ET0/01)
assessment.content: Section A: Shakespeare (school text: Macbeth), 40 marks. Section B: post-1914 British play or novel (school text: An Inspector Calls), 40 marks including 8 for AO4.
assessment.format: Closed book. Section A: part (a) close analysis of an extract of about 30 lines (20 marks, AO2); part (b) the same theme elsewhere in the play (20 marks, AO1 and AO3). Section B: one essay from a choice of two.

assessment.title: 19th-century Novel and Poetry since 1789 (1ET0/02)
assessment.content: Section A: 19th-century novel (school text: A Christmas Carol), 40 marks. Section B: Part 1 anthology poetry comparison (Conflict collection), 20 marks; Part 2 two unseen contemporary poems compared, 20 marks.
assessment.format: Closed book. Section A: extract of about 400 words analysed (20 marks, AO2), then an essay on the whole novel (20 marks, AO1). Section B: compare a named anthology poem with another from the collection; compare two unseen poems linked by theme.

nonExam: None. Both papers are closed book: no texts are allowed in the examination.

aos.desc: Read, understand and respond to texts with a critical style and an informed personal response, using references and quotations.
Analyse language, form and structure to create meanings and effects, using subject terminology.
Show understanding of the relationships between texts and the contexts in which they were written.
Use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures with accurate spelling and punctuation.

units.title: Component 1 Section B: Post-1914 British play: An Inspector Calls (J.B. Priestley)
points: Know the whole play: plot, characters, setting and structure.
Explore themes such as responsibility, class, age and gender.
Relate the play to its contexts: written 1945, set 1912.
Write one essay from a choice of two, each opened by a short quotation.
Spelling, punctuation and grammar are assessed in this section (AO4, 8 marks).
units.foundingYear: Not taught in 2027 (TGA opens in January): taught from Autumn 2027, as in the school's booklet.

units.title: Component 2 Section A: 19th-century novel: A Christmas Carol (Charles Dickens)
points: Know the whole novella: plot, characters, setting and structure.
Analyse language, form and structure in an extract of about 400 words (AO2).
Write an essay on the whole text: plot, setting, character or theme (AO1).
Understand Victorian contexts: poverty, the Poor Law, charity and redemption.

units.title: Component 2 Section B Part 1: Poetry Anthology, Conflict collection: poems 1 to 6
points: Study the first six poems of the Conflict collection in the Pearson Poetry Anthology.
Analyse language, form and structure in each poem.
Relate each poem to its context.
Compare a named poem with another poem from the collection.

units.title: Component 1 Section A: Shakespeare: Macbeth
points: Know the whole play: plot, characters, themes and structure.
Part (a): analyse language, form and structure in an extract of about 30 lines (AO2).
Part (b): explore how a theme from the extract appears elsewhere in the play (AO1, AO3).
Understand Jacobean contexts: kingship, the supernatural and James I.

units.title: Component 2 Section B Part 1: Poetry Anthology, Conflict collection: the remaining nine poems
points: Study the remaining nine poems, so all 15 poems of the collection are covered, as the specification requires.
Compare poems across the collection on theme and method.
Practise the comparison question against the mark scheme.

units.title: Component 2 Section B Part 2: Unseen poetry
points: Compare two unseen contemporary poems linked by a theme.
Analyse how each poet presents the theme through language, form and structure.
Build a timed method for reading and comparing unseen poems.

units.title: Year 11 revision: Macbeth, A Christmas Carol, An Inspector Calls and the Conflict collection
points: Autumn: revise Macbeth alongside Language Paper 1 and A Christmas Carol alongside Language Paper 2; November mocks.
Spring: revise An Inspector Calls; conflict and unseen poetry during Ramadan; second mock assessments.
Closed book: learn key quotations for every set text.
units.foundingYear: Founding-year Year 11 joins in January: covered in the Spring 1 catch-up and revision, as far as the cohort needs (to confirm with each pupil's prior school).

commandWords.meaning: Examine how a writer presents an idea, theme or character.
Set two poems side by side on ideas and methods.
Discuss several methods a writer uses and their effects.

skills: Close analysis of language, form and structure in extracts.
Essay writing on whole texts with embedded quotation.
Using context to explain a writer's choices.

prerequisites.from: Year 7 Frankenstein and Year 9 The Woman in Black (Gothic, 19th-century style)

links.how: The booklet pairs A Christmas Carol revision with Language Paper 2 and Macbeth with Paper 1.

links.topic: Victorian poverty and the Edwardian class system
links.how: History supplies the contexts of 1912 and 1945 and of Victorian London.

contextNote: Set texts are the school's: Macbeth, An Inspector Calls, A Christmas Carol and the Conflict collection. Teach them as literature, with Islamic perspectives on justice, charity and responsibility where they fit.
